**Verdict: ready.** No blockers. Two notes.

Read-only review: diff, the three test files on this head and on `c31384ae4^1`, `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/stamp.rs` and `crates/post/src/post/mod.rs` `dump` on `origin/main`.

## What each test protects now

The law: a rapid never changes the tool pose. Each test walks all moves with `held = m.axis.or(held)` and does `assert_eq!(m.axis, held)` on each rapid. This includes the opening rapid, the rapids between passes and the exit rapids.

- `crates/motion/tests/multiaxis.rs:171` `rapids_hold_the_pose_they_inherit` (memory at line 182, lean check at lines 180-181).
- `crates/motion/tests/multiaxis_avoid.rs:154` `dodging_never_moves_the_ball` (lean check at line 175, memory at line 176).
- `crates/motion/tests/multiaxis_rough.rs:140` `rapids_and_floors_hold_no_pose_and_flanks_do` (memory at line 162; the lean is proved by `flanks >= 4`).

The stamp agrees with this walk (`stamp.rs` lines 204-224):
- After the first lean, a rapid gets `Some(held)`, and `held` is the last stated pose.
- Before the first lean, each `None` becomes `Some(UP)` only when the path leans.

Thus the start value `Some(UP)` is the pose that the post commands on the first stated move. It is not a loaded answer. If the first rapid stated a tilt, `assert_eq!(Some(tilt), Some(UP))` fails. If a rapid after a lean stated upright, the assert also fails. The test still catches the two failure modes.

The added "the path leans" asserts are correct. Without them, a path with no pose (all `None`) fails at the first rapid (`None != Some(UP)`) and does not pass silently. The asserts make the failure message clear. In `multiaxis_rough` the flank count does the same work.

Floor law in `multiaxis_rough`: it is kept. Each non-vertical pose of a cut must be within the cone of a horizontal seed and must have `a.z == 0` (lines 170-187). A tilted floor fails one of the two checks.

## Product check (post `dump`, `origin/main` lines 430-565)

- `leans && !commanded` writes `A0 B0` (zero angles) one time, on the first stated Z column.
- Then `commanded` is true. The later upright moves before the first lean write no rotary word (`abc = None`), because `tilted` is false.
- After a lean, the first upright move writes the zero angles one time (`tilted`).
- No repeated rotary words come from the upright moves before the lean. No rate is computed for a move with `abc = None`. So a late first lean in Multi-Axis Rough does not cause new words or a rate refusal.

## Scope

- Only the three test files change (18 insertions, 6 deletions). No product file changes.
- The `#[test]` count is the same: 7, 6 and 5. The `ignore` count is the same (1 in each file, not touched).
- No assertion is removed or made weaker.

## Notes (not blockers)

1. `crates/motion/tests/multiaxis_rough.rs`: the name and two comments state the old law.
   - Line 140: the name says "floors hold no pose". Floors and rapids now state the upright pose.
   - Line 146: "(axis None)".
   - Line 184: "Floors pose nothing".
   A name such as `rapids_hold_their_pose_floors_stand_upright_and_flanks_lean` is correct. A follow-up `P7` is sufficient.
2. The one legal exception (the opening move commands upright from an unknown machine pose) is in the start value of the memory. The tests do not assert it directly. A direct check is: the first move with a stated pose is a rapid at the clearance height, with `Some(UP)`. This is optional hardening for the same `P7` follow-up.

## Built

Built: not built by this review. The author's readings on this head:
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion` (debug): 136 binaries ok (lib 538; `multiaxis` 7; `multiaxis_avoid` 6; `multiaxis_rough` 5).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Post-merge run 45036812289 on c31384ae4: 1092 steps, only these 3 FAIL.

Body: `Changelog: none` (test-only change, correct), `Fixes #3486`, `Refs #3300`.

Coordinator: this PR merges now. It is the fix for a red main (#3486).

- Class: no refresh. The PR merges cleanly with `main`. It changes three test files of `crates/motion/tests/` and no product file.
- Review: comment 7081888719 on this exact head 51e830f25 (ready).
- Gate: the author ran the whole `camcraft-motion` crate in debug on this head (136 binaries, all passed; `multiaxis` 7, `multiaxis_avoid` 6, `multiaxis_rough` 5) and clippy for motion (clean). The red run 45036812289 ran all 1092 steps of the batch tier with only these three failures, so no other suite was red. No heavy lane applies to a change of three default test files with no product change.
- The two notes of the review (the old test name and two comments in `multiaxis_rough.rs`; a direct assert that the first posed move is an upright rapid at the clearance) go to a `P7` follow-up issue.
